LESSON: MAP READING AND INTERPRETATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Map Reading and Interpretation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Map Reading and Interpretation, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY.

Key inquiry question: How do we read and interpret topographical maps?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Brainstorm on meaning and types of maps and share in class. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC or

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Brainstorm on meaning and types of maps and share in class. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC or

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Map Reading and Interpretation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: The skill of self-awareness and planning as the learner draws sketch sections from topographical

maps and display in class

● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with technology as the learner watches video clips on relief, drainage,

and vegetation and take notes

● Critical Thinking :The skill of interpretation and inference as the learner discusses how relief, drainage and

vegetation are interpreted on topographical maps and make class presentations

● Communication and Collaboration: The skill of teamwork is enhanced as learners use print or digital

resources, in groups, to research on the various methods of representing relief on topographical maps and draw

sketches.

● Creativity and Imagination: The skill of making connections is enhanced as learners draw sketch sections from

topographical maps and display in class.

Values:
• Unity: Learner strives to achieve a common goal as they use print or digital resources to research on the various

methods of representing relief on topographical maps and draws sketches

• Respect: Learner respects diverse opinions as they discuss how relief, drainage and vegetation are interpreted on

topographical maps and makes class presentations

• Responsibility: Learner takes care of digital devices as they watch video clips on relief, drainage and vegetation

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self-Awareness: Learner engages in work shadowing on a possible career in Geography and shares

experiences in class

● Creative Thinking: Learner creates a poster on careers related to Geography and displays in school

● Social Cohesion: Learner works with others as they brainstorm on the importance of statistics in Geography.

● Environmental Education as learners conduct a digital or library research on the significance of Geography in

day-to-day life and present in class.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Approved textbooks and other printed resources ,photographs, pictures ,digital resources, library ,display boards
